=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: Lines 12672-12674 (managed) and 14857-14859 (standalone) | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Both recovery arms use a `comments(last: 100)` cache without detecting truncation, so an unresolved staged-support latch older than the cache window is treated as absent and auto-approval proceeds.
  WHY: After enough comments accumulate following the latch, `max_by(event_key)` finds no latch and the guard returns “no unresolved latch”; the severity was consistently reported as MAJOR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: Line 14862, standalone REST fallback `|| echo '[]'` | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The standalone REST fallback converts comments-fetch failures into `[]`, causing an unavailable comment history to be interpreted as no unresolved latch and allowing auto-approval.
  WHY: A failed REST read after the GraphQL cache misses bypasses the intended fail-closed `rc=2` path; the severity was consistently reported as MAJOR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: line 12678 (managed fallback, new in this run) | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: The managed REST fallback can also turn a clean `gh` failure into an empty array because `jq -s` succeeds on empty input, so the fail-closed path is unreachable for that failure mode.
  WHY: The managed guard can likewise auto-approve when the comments read fails; qwen_qwen3_7-plus disagreed and described the managed behavior as correct, but the highest reported severity is MAJOR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: 12548-12567 (jq -e exit code handling in _staged_support_latch_release_incomplete) | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `_staged_support_latch_release_incomplete` returns raw `jq -e` error codes, while callers special-case only 0 and 2, so other jq errors fall through to auto-approval.
  WHY: Unexpected jq failures are treated as “no unresolved latch” instead of fail-closed; confidence differed across reviewers, so the maximum confidence is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: Line 14745 (compensation-failure `tg_notify_issue` CRITICAL alert text) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: The CRITICAL alert says only standalone recovery will not auto-approve even though the managed arm is also guarded.
  WHY: The alert is stale relative to the shipped behavior and understates containment; no runtime failure was reported.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 12670-12687 (managed arm, new in this run) and 14896-14906 (standalone arm) | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: The marker-only guard cannot distinguish a half-applied automated release from completed manual remediation without an `ai:needs-human-auto-release` marker, causing permanent auto-approval skips after certain manual remediations.
  WHY: A manually remediated issue can remain blocked indefinitely until someone posts `/approved`.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 12672-12674 (managed) and 14857-14859 (standalone) — GraphQL cache from `_fetch_candidate_issue_details_graphql` carrying `comments(last: 100)` at line 13839
  Problem: The shared `_staged_support_latch_release_incomplete` function is the only guard preventing auto-approval of a half-released staged-support latch, but both the managed and standalone recovery arms feed it from the `comments(last: 100)` GraphQL cache when the issue is present in that cache. The conditional `if [ -n "${_current_wave_details_json}" ] && jq -e 'has($n)'` at line 12672 and the matching standalone guard at line 14857 use the cache first; the paginated REST fallback is reached only when the issue is absent from the cache, not when the cache simply lacks the relevant comment. Once the latch comment ages beyond the 100-comment window, `max_by(event_key)` finds no latch and the function returns 1 ("no unresolved latch"), so stall recovery posts `/approved` and resumes implementation.
  Why it fails at runtime: After the double-failure contingency the issue sits in `ai:awaiting-approval`. Each poll cycle adds at least one orchestrator comment; after ~100 cycles (or faster if the issue has other churn) the latch comment exits the window, the guard silently degrades, and the issue is auto-approved despite an unresolved human gate.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: Line 14862, standalone REST fallback `|| echo '[]'`
  Problem: When the standalone recovery path misses the GraphQL cache and falls back to REST, the `|| echo '[]'` on line 14862 explicitly coerces every failure mode (including `gh_retry` exhausting all retries) into a valid empty JSON array `[]`.
  Why it fails at runtime: Stall recovery then auto-approves.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: Line 14745, compensation-failure `tg_notify_issue` CRITICAL alert text
  Problem: The alert says "ai:awaiting-approval remains, but standalone stall recovery will not auto-approve while the staged-support latch marker is unresolved." This round's diff added the managed-arm guard at lines 12670-12687.
  Why it fails at runtime: No runtime failure. The alert understates the containment.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 12548-12567, `_staged_support_latch_release_incomplete` jq -e exit codes
  Problem: The inner `jq -e` pipeline can return exit codes 0 (true), 1 (false/null), or 3-5 (compile error, runtime error, etc.). Callers at lines 12680 and 14898 check only for rc=0 or rc=2.
  Why it fails at runtime: A jq error falls through both checks and reaches the auto-approve code, treating it as "no unresolved latch."
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 12672-12674 (managed arm, new in this run) and 14857-14859 (standalone arm), both consuming the `_fetch_candidate_issue_details_graphql` cache whose projection is `comments(last: 100)` at line 13839 (`_current_wave_details_json` is populated from the same helper at line 18487)
  Problem: `_staged_support_latch_release_incomplete` is the only guard preventing generic auto-approval of a half-released staged-support latch, but on the cache-hit path it evaluates at most the 100 newest comments.
  Why it fails at runtime: after the double-failure contingency, an issue that accumulates 100+ comments past the latch comment is auto-approved by managed or standalone stall recovery even though the staged-support human gate was never resolved.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 12670-12687 (managed arm, new in this run) and 14896-14906 (standalone arm)
  Problem: The guard keys only on comment markers: any trusted staged-support latch comment with no trusted release marker after it blocks auto-approve forever.
  Why it fails at runtime: after manual remediation without a release marker, the issue stalls at `ai:awaiting-approval` and every automated auto-approve is skipped indefinitely; only a manual `/approved` comment unblocks it.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: line 12678 (managed fallback, new in this run) and line 14862 (standalone fallback)
  Problem: Both REST fallbacks convert a clean `gh` failure into a valid empty comments array.
  Why it fails at runtime: a transient GitHub API failure on the comments read silently disables the fail-closed path and both recovery arms auto-approve an issue whose staged-support latch is unresolved.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: `_staged_support_latch_release_incomplete` (lines 12542-12568) and its callers (12680-12687, 14897-14905)
  Problem: The function returns the raw exit code of the second `jq -e`. Callers special-case only 0 (incomplete latch) and 2 (unavailable); every other code — including jq internal error codes 3/4/5 — is treated as 1, "no latch, safe to approve".
  Why it fails at runtime: a jq internal error on valid comment JSON takes the auto-approve path rather than the documented fail-closed `staged_support_latch_comments_unavailable` skip.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

  Problem: The alert still says "standalone stall recovery will not auto-approve while the staged-support latch marker is unresolved", but this run added the managed-arm guard (lines 12670-12687).
  Why it fails at runtime: no runtime failure; the alert text is stale relative to the behavior this run shipped.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 12542-12568 (_staged_support_latch_release_incomplete function), 14862 (standalone REST fallback)
  Problem: The standalone REST fallback at line 14862 uses `|| echo '[]'` which produces a valid empty JSON array on failure.
  Why it fails at runtime: The function receives '[]', treats it as "no latch found" instead of "comments unavailable", and allows generic stall recovery to post `/approved` and resume implement.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 12548-12567 (jq -e exit code handling in _staged_support_latch_release_incomplete)
  Problem: The function returns the raw exit code of `jq -e`, which can be 0 (true), 1 (false), or >1 (jq error such as parse failure or internal error).
  Why it fails at runtime: The caller's conditional checks both fail, so execution continues to the auto-approval path.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 12678 (managed REST fallback), 14862 (standalone REST fallback)
  Problem: The managed and standalone REST fallbacks use different failure handlers: managed uses `|| printf ''` while standalone uses `|| echo '[]'`.
  Why it fails at runtime: The standalone arm's error handling is incorrect; when the REST API fails, it should treat it as "comments unavailable" and skip auto-approval.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 12539-12568 (function documentation), 13839 (GraphQL comments query)
  Problem: The function documentation states "Return 0 when a trusted staged-support latch has no trusted release after it, 1 when no unresolved latch exists, and 2 for malformed comment input", but the GraphQL cache only fetches `comments(last: 100)`.
  Why it fails at runtime: An issue with 100+ comments after the latch has the latch outside the cache window, so the function returns 1 and the caller proceeds with auto-approval.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
